blurb: Civil War scholars have ignored or dismissed the importance of the cotton trade in Texas. But in fact one-third of all the cotton that left the Confederacy was Texas cotton. Texas and Confederate agencies secured more than $478 million from cotton sales, shipping to buyers in Europe and the northern States. Confederate officials, aware of this, tried to harness the profits for the support of their military.
